Subject: Post-demo: Flowlytics sample query bank & eval constraints

Hi Joanna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our demo and a small request to help us scope an evaluation that reflects Flowlytics' production workload.

What we heard on the call (high level):
- Most calls are multi-step workflows (user asks -> system clarifies -> follow-ups).
- ~35% of queries contain account or PII-like identifiers (order ids, device ids).
- Tight latency constraints for web UI (p50 < 250ms target).

What we need from you to run a focused model-fit eval:
1) A sample query bank (CSV or JSON) with ~150–300 representative queries. Please include a short label for each (e.g., "billing_issue", "device_sync_error", "intent:faq").
2) A short list of edge cases (~15–25) that break current accuracy: ambiguous intents, chained clarifications, and cases requiring multi-step reasoning.
3) Any redaction guidance or regulatory limits (PII redaction rules, fields that must never leave Flowlytics tenancy).

Deliverable we will return: a one-page eval summary with recommended model variants (latency vs. quality tradeoffs), a small prompt set for A/B testing, and a suggested redaction policy mapping.

Next steps: if you can drop the sample_prompts.csv (or a Drive link) by Wednesday EOD, we’ll run a 3-day bench and come back with a short readout and recommended model candidates. Also include the person to loop in for procurement if needed.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample_prompts.csv (stub)

Quick notes:
- The CSV contains 120 rows; each row has: example_text, label, product_area, severity. We redacted customer_account_id already, replacing with {{ACCOUNT_ID}}.
- Edge cases: included 18 cases that routinely cause our current NLU to misroute. Those are marked with label EDGECASE in the CSV.
- For compliance: any token that looks like a 10+ digit numeric id must be redacted; device serials are sensitive and should not be stored in plain text.

One ask from our side: can Redwood provide suggested redaction regex patterns (we can run pre-filtering before sharing more data)? Also curious what model families you expect to test — latency will be crucial.

Hannah / Karthik — I reviewed Joanna's CSV and redaction note. Quick plan and model recommendations so we can turn this around in ~72 hours: 

Plan:
- Ingest the CSV with a synthetic-redaction pass to preserve intent tokens but remove raw identifiers. We can use placeholder mapping (we should ask Flowlytics to keep the {{ACCOUNT_ID}} pattern).
- Produce three eval tracks: 
  A) Latency-priority (cheap quantized model) — aim for p50 < 200ms: candidates: rwinfer-lite-3b-quant, open-lite-3b-q8
  B) Balanced (quality + moderate cost): rwinfer-standard-7b, rwinfer-7b-q4
  C) Quality-first (higher latency/cost): rwinfer-hf-13b, open-13b-raw

Notes on QA and regression risk:
- Edge cases with multi-step clarifications will likely show biggest delta between A and C. We should surface per-label F1 and a small suite of behavioral tests (clarification-preserve, slot-extraction, routing-precision).
- We'll seed a small prompt kit (10 templates) covering clarifications and follow-ups, and run LM prompts with and without prefix caching to measure delta on token cost.

Immediate asks for Hannah:
1) Confirm we have permission to synthetically redact (replace numeric ids with placeholders) and store the redacted set in our ephemeral eval environment.
2) If yes, route the Procurement contact at Flowlytics to me so I can start the SOW/committed eval consumables if needed.

I can draft the eval-run checklist and runbook tonight. If you want, we can include a short bake-off plan in the HubSpot deal notes (FL-9201).

—Ben

2) Deliverables and timeline: once we have your sign-off on redaction, Ben's team will run the three-track eval and return:
   - 1-page model tradeoff summary (latency, cost, per-label F1)
   - 10-template prompt kit for A/B testing
   - A short redaction checklist mapping (we attached a draft: redaction-checklist.pdf)

3) Action items for Flowlytics: please confirm procurement contact (copied) and whether you can add an additional ~30 edge-case examples across products (preferred as a separate CSV column). Those examples help us stress the clarification flows.

4) I scheduled a 30-min readout for Friday 11am PT (tentative) — confirm if that works. If you prefer earlier, we can accelerate.

Thanks again — looking forward to running this.
